original_test_intent: Visually verify OSFP Channel 2 indication for functional, I/O-active and non-functional conditions, while leaving the explicitly undefined Amber Blink state for engineering disposition.
original_method: A qualified on-site operator identifies the exact CH2 cage and lane group, applies only approved functional and non-functional states plus bounded CH2 traffic, records LED color/cadence, and restores the optical path.
manual_activity: An on-site operator labels OSFP CH2, executes the approved functional, CH2-I/O and safe non-functional matrix, captures contextual and close video, records Amber Blink as unresolved, and verifies recovery.
required_inputs: Exact OSFP CH2 cage/channel/lane map, module serial/PN/FW and peer endpoint
Definition of functional state including module presence, link, lane, FEC and service health
Safe reproducible non-functional stimulus and recovery that does not damage optics or strand management
Bounded CH2-specific I/O stimulus plus expected green blink frequency/duty and observation time
Amber Solid fault class, assertion timing and expected link/module telemetry
Engineering disposition for undefined Amber Blink by hardware/FW revision
LED legend, viewing/color reference and timestamped evidence standard
Passive CMIS/module/link/FEC/error sources and independent fabric recovery
safety_requirements: Verify CH2 labels, module and peer before any stimulus; software enumeration is not a physical label
Do not create a non-functional state by unapproved optical removal, transmitter disable, loopback, fault injection or power action
Follow laser and ESD safety and never view an exposed optical transmitter
Pin test traffic to CH2 and prove it did not fail over through CH1
Do not convert undefined Amber Blink into an inferred acceptance state
Stop on failed link recovery, increasing FEC/error counts, module alarm, thermal/power anomaly or ambiguous LED target
agent_execution_scope: Verify the exact source and CH2 physical/logical topology
Prepare the approved state/stimulus matrix and observation checklist
Collect passive module identity, CMIS status, channel/link/FEC/error and event evidence before and after
Timestamp-correlate operator visual evidence without interpreting unseen color or cadence
Perform no module handling, optical fault, traffic generation, link control, reset, power action, automatic retry or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve CH2 identity and functional/non-functional definitions
Approve safe CH2 traffic and fault stimulus with restoration
Define green cadence, Amber Solid mapping and revision-scoped Amber Blink disposition
Review visual plus telemetry evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly states no remote command can establish visual LED acceptance; it omits safe stimuli, CH2 identity and undefined-state disposition.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use an operator-controlled CH2 state matrix with synchronized video and passive module/lane/link/FEC telemetry; separately approve any traffic or fault action.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: OSFP CH2, Green Solid/Blink, Amber Solid and undefined Amber Blink plus 15/5-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL CH2 VISUAL REVIEW REQUIRES CHANNEL-BOUND TRAFFIC, SAFE FAULT SEMANTICS AND DIRECT EVIDENCE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map the physical indicator to CH2 lanes/module/peer, synchronize video to the approved state timeline, and corroborate the observation with passive lane-specific CMIS/link/FEC data.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact CH2 identity, bounded state transitions, cadence measurement and recovery proof without replacing direct observation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Passive telemetry supports the observation but cannot establish visible color or blinking; CH1 is a different checkpoint and Amber Blink remains undefined.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A shared OSFP housing may expose aggregate module status while CH2 lanes are idle or degraded. Without channel-bound traffic and lane evidence, a correct-looking LED can reflect CH1 or whole-module health rather than the channel under test.

project_override_considerations: If hardware provides only a module-level LED, engineering must define how CH2 contributes to the aggregate and whether this row has unique acceptance. Amber Blink can become N/A only through revision-scoped approval.
expected_evidence: Approved CH2 cage/lane/module/peer mapping and state definitions
Safe stimulus, green cadence, Amber Solid mapping and Amber Blink disposition
Timestamped contextual and close photo/video showing CH2 identity and stimulus timeline
Passive pre/post module/CMIS/lane/link/FEC/error/event evidence and restored service

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria agree on green and amber state names, and explicitly state that Amber Blink is not defined. The missing behavior is retained as unresolved coverage rather than treated as a contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The CH2 visual purpose and defined states can be executed manually after project inputs are approved. Amber Blink remains pending and does not invalidate the static review.

review_improvement: Adds CH2 physical/logical identity, lane-bound stimulus proof, optical safety limits and recovery evidence while preserving direct visual ownership and all original states.
independent_technical_reasoning: OSFP channel numbering is platform-specific and may describe a lane group inside a shared module rather than a distinct pluggable. The reviewer must therefore correlate the physical CH2 label with the platform lane map and traffic counters; a blinking aggregate module LED during unrelated CH1 traffic is not evidence for this case.
